question: Which kind of entries may a custom fill list contain directly according to the lecture?
options: Text or text mixed with numbers
explanation: The lecture permits custom list entries made from text, including labels combining letters and digits. Numeric-only lists are not entered by the same manual custom-list workflow. Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.67. Check whether entries already exist in cells before choosing the workflow.

question: A fictional ward-name list already exists in worksheet cells. Which button brings the selected cell range into Custom Lists?
explanation: Import reads list items from the referenced worksheet cell range into the Custom Lists dialog. Add is used for manually typed entries; Delete removes a selected custom list. Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.69. Check whether entries already exist in cells before choosing the workflow.

question: Which choice begins creating a list by typing its entries?
explanation: The NEW LIST choice opens an empty custom-list entry area. After entering items in their desired order, the lecturer instructs users to choose Add. Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.72. Check whether entries already exist in cells before choosing the workflow.

question: You have finished typing a new custom list in its intended order. Which action stores those typed entries?
explanation: Add saves the text entered in the List entries box as a new custom list. Import is used when the items are already present in worksheet cells. Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.73. Check whether entries already exist in cells before choosing the workflow.

question: A formula using cell addresses is difficult to interpret. What benefit does replacing suitable references with descriptive range names provide?
explanation: A meaningful range name can express the purpose of the referenced cells, making complex formulas easier to read and maintain. Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.118. A readable name still needs to refer to the intended cells.

question: Which name meets the slide’s stated starting-character rule?
explanation: The slide permits a name to start with an underscore. A leading digit or space does not meet its stated range-naming rule. Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.119. A readable name still needs to refer to the intended cells.

question: Where is the Name Box located?
options: At the left end of the Formula Bar
explanation: The Name Box appears to the left of the Formula bar and displays the active reference or assigned range name. Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.121. A readable name still needs to refer to the intended cells.

question: A worksheet needs several descriptive range names. Which tool does the lecturer recommend instead of repeatedly using Define Name?
explanation: Name Manager is used to inspect and manage named ranges. It is useful when a workbook contains several defined names. Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.126. A readable name still needs to refer to the intended cells.

question: A fictional worksheet is named CSM 1 and its required value is in A10. Which reference correctly addresses that cell?
explanation: The sheet name contains a space, so it is enclosed in single quotes. An exclamation point separates 'CSM 1' from the A10 address. Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.102. Distinguish a worksheet span from a cell-address range.

question: Which symbol separates a worksheet name from its cell reference?
explanation: An exclamation mark joins a worksheet name to the referenced cell or range, for example Sheet2!A1 or a quoted sheet name followed by !A1. Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.102. Distinguish a worksheet span from a cell-address range.

question: What does the sheet range in Sheet1:Sheet4!D1 specify?
explanation: The colon connects the first and last worksheet in a three-dimensional reference, covering Sheet1, Sheet2, Sheet3 and Sheet4 in order. Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.104. Distinguish a worksheet span from a cell-address range.

question: Four worksheets, Sheet1 through Sheet4, each contain monthly amounts in D1:D10. Which formula totals that range across the worksheet span?
explanation: SUM(Sheet1:Sheet4!D1:D10) adds matching D1:D10 cells across every worksheet from Sheet1 through Sheet4, which is a 3-D reference. Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.104. Distinguish a worksheet span from a cell-address range.

question: A fictional register stores identifiers down the first column and related values across each row. Which function matches that search direction?
explanation: VLOOKUP looks for its lookup value in the first column of the referenced table and returns a result from a specified column. Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.203. This glossary does not supply a complete lookup-argument tutorial.

question: A fictional table stores lookup keys across its top row. Which function matches that search direction?
explanation: HLOOKUP examines the top row of a table and returns a value from a specified row in the matching column. Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.203. This glossary does not supply a complete lookup-argument tutorial.

question: Which function returns a matching item's relative position?
explanation: MATCH reports the relative position at which a lookup value is found, rather than returning the value from a different column. Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.203. This glossary does not supply a complete lookup-argument tutorial.

question: Which function switches rows and columns?
explanation: TRANSPOSE swaps the orientation of rows and columns, allowing a horizontal arrangement to become vertical or vice versa. Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.203. This glossary does not supply a complete lookup-argument tutorial.

question: Several regional sales sheets must be combined onto one summary sheet. What is the destination called in the lecture?
explanation: Consolidation collects data from multiple source ranges on one master or summary worksheet. (PDF p.305) Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.305. The destination, inputs and fixed/linked choice have distinct roles.

question: When using Excel Consolidate, what is the role of the destination range?
options: Location where the combined results appear
Range containing each original data source
explanation: The destination is where the consolidated output is placed. Source references identify the contributing data. (PDF p.306) Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.306. The destination, inputs and fixed/linked choice have distinct roles.

question: Linked consolidation results use several source worksheets. A source value subsequently changes. What may happen to the linked results?
explanation: Create Links to Source Data can allow updated consolidated results as source data changes. (PDF p.309) Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.309. The destination, inputs and fixed/linked choice have distinct roles.

question: A fictional SUM consolidation combines monthly totals of 12, 15 and 23. What is the result?
explanation: SUM adds the matching values: 12+15+23 = 50. This created arithmetic illustration does not choose any official payroll rates.

question: A printed worksheet needs a horizontal page break after a particular row. Where should the active cell be before inserting it?
options: On the row header of the printed title
At the last column of the worksheet
explanation: Place the active cell in the row immediately below the desired horizontal split, then insert a manual page break. Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.272. The active cell is below a horizontal boundary; the values themselves are not moved.

question: What do manual page breaks do relative to automatic breaks?
options: Delete cells at the break positions
Remove the need for a print area
explanation: Manual breaks influence pagination and cause Excel to reposition its automatically determined breaks. Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.272. Changing pagination changes printed boundaries, not the source records.

question: Which Page Setup tab does the source associate with print titles and page order?
explanation: The source lists print area, print titles and page order under Sheet. Page concerns orientation/size, while margins and headers have other roles.

question: A worksheet needs its title and page number at the top of every printed page. Which feature fits?
options: A new data row on every page
explanation: A header can place repeated information at the top of printed pages without inserting false observations into the data table.

question: A title is in a placeholder and another label is in a text box. What does the source say about text formatting?
options: Both can use the same text-formatting commands
Text boxes must be converted into tables first
Formatting a text box always changes every slide
explanation: The source explicitly says text in placeholders and text boxes can be formatted using the same commands. Container type does not require converting text to a table.

question: Center alignment is applied to text in a small box near the slide edge. What is centred?
options: The box itself across the whole slide
The presentation within the application window
explanation: Text alignment acts within the placeholder or text box. It does not reposition the container itself on the slide.

question: Why can the available background styles change after applying a different theme?
options: They are fixed to the file name
Every theme deletes all existing pictures
They are fill variations based on theme colours
The slide count determines background colours
explanation: The source links background styles to theme colours. A new theme can therefore change their available colour variations.

question: A slide lists seven procedures that must be followed in order. Which list format best conveys their sequence?
explanation: Numbering conveys an ordered sequence; bullet symbols identify items without necessarily implying order. (PDF p.453) Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.454. Numbered points show sequence; an unordered bullet list does not explicitly number the steps.

question: A continued procedure list should begin at 4. Which field in the described numbering dialog sets that value?
explanation: The lecturer identifies the Start at field for a numbered list. Font size and line spacing change appearance rather than its initial number.

question: Which text-alignment option lines up text with both the left and right container margins?
explanation: The source describes Justify as lining text up equally to both margins. This differs from centring lines or aligning only one side.

question: Which key does the source name for moving the insertion point between table cells?
explanation: The table navigation slide names Tab, with the mouse and arrow keys as other ways to move. This is a source-described behavior, not a newly executed PowerPoint keyboard check.

question: An existing PowerPoint table needs one additional row immediately above the selected row. Where does the lecturer direct you?
explanation: The lecture places Insert Above in the Rows & Columns group of the contextual Table Tools Layout tab. (PDF p.459) Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.460. Insert Above is relative to the insertion-point row; it is different from a slide insertion.

question: A PowerPoint table needs a new column immediately to the right of the current one. Which command fits?
explanation: The source distinguishes left/right column insertion from above/below row insertion. Merging cells does not add the requested column.

question: The colour of a picture border is correct but its line is too thin. Which setting changes its width?
explanation: Picture Border includes a Weight setting for line width. The other settings affect audio, slide changes or text spacing.

question: A picture became stretched after resizing. Which source-described action can change its proportions?
options: Moving the whole picture without resizing it
explanation: The source warns that side sizing handles do not keep the same proportions. Moving the picture or changing unrelated settings does not itself explain this distortion.

question: During a slide show, an inserted sound is too loud. Which Audio Tools option directly changes playback loudness?
explanation: The Audio Tools options in the slides identify Volume as the loudness control; loop, hiding and timing affect other aspects of playback. (PDF p.510) Reconciled citation: actual 542-page lecturer PDF p.511. Volume changes loudness; looping and icon visibility concern different playback options.

question: Which print-output choice is intended to put several slides on one sheet?
explanation: The source distinguishes handouts with multiple slides per page from notes pages and on-screen editing views. The number of slides per page is a separate choice.

question: A presenter wants printed speaker notes with the relevant slide. Which output fits?
explanation: The source names Notes Pages for typed speaker notes. A handout layout or file name does not by itself include those notes.

question: Only specified slides should be printed. Which print-range choice fits?
explanation: Custom Range selects the intended subset. Copy count changes repetitions of the output, not which slides belong in it.

question: The transition on a slide should be removed. Which option does the later source example choose?
explanation: The later transition example selects None. Theme changes and extra slides are unrelated to removing the between-slide effect.

question: Two effects on the same slide play in the wrong sequence. What should be reordered?
options: The animation effects for that slide
The slides rather than their effects
explanation: The source describes reordering effects in the animation list. Slide order and effect order are different; changing slides does not directly fix two effects on one slide.

question: Which source-described field controls automatic advancement to the next slide after an interval?
explanation: The timing example uses Automatically After for advancing slides. Legacy tab names differ in the notes, and actual target-version timing still requires the pending desktop test.
